podcast.body: The Rolling Stones' "Satisfaction" became a massive hit and solidified the distorted guitar sound's place at the forefront of rock music. The iconic riff, initially intended by Keith Richards to be a placeholder for a horn section and played with a Maestro Fuzz tone, was loved by the rest of the band despite Richards' preference for horns. Recorded at RCA Studios in Hollywood on May 12, 1965, the song was released four weeks later. "Another satisfaction was a hit for the Stones. Everybody wanted a Maestro Fuzz tone, but key thritchards almost didn't use that bit."
